data.title: Build a Plant Leaf Cell
data.description: Explore the inside of a plant leaf cell by placing its organelles in the correct zones and learning what they do!

organelles.name: Nucleus
organelles.function: It is the control center of the cell and holds DNA.
organelles.analogy: Like the principal's office in a school.
organelles.quantityReasoning: A plant cell only needs one main control center to direct all its daily activities.

organelles.name: Mitochondria
organelles.function: They make energy for the cell to use.
organelles.quantityReasoning: Leaf cells need energy to live and grow, so they have several power-generating mitochondria.

organelles.name: Chloroplast
organelles.function: They capture sunlight to make food for the plant through photosynthesis.
organelles.quantityReasoning: Leaf cells capture lots of sunlight to make food, so they need many solar-panel chloroplasts.

organelles.name: Large Central Vacuole
organelles.function: It stores water and helps keep the plant cell firm.
organelles.quantityReasoning: Plant cells usually have one huge central water tank to help hold the plant upright.

organelles.name: Cytoplasm
organelles.function: It is the jelly-like fluid that fills the cell and holds parts in place.
organelles.analogy: Like fruit jelly inside a donut.
organelles.quantityReasoning: The cell needs enough fluid to fill all the space and cushion the internal parts.

organelles.name: Cell Membrane
organelles.function: It controls what goes in and out of the cell.
organelles.analogy: Like a security guard at a door.
organelles.quantityReasoning: Every cell surrounds itself with one protective outer wrapper.

organelles.name: Centrioles
organelles.function: They help organize cell division in animal cells.
organelles.distractorExplanation: Centrioles are typically only found in animal cells, not plant cells.

organelles.name: Lysosome
organelles.function: They break down waste and old cell parts.
organelles.distractorExplanation: Lysosomes are very rare in plant cells and belong mostly in animal cells.

functionMatches.functionDescription: Acts as the brain of the cell by storing instructions and telling other parts what to do.
Converts nutrients into usable energy so the cell can perform its daily tasks.
Uses energy from the sun to turn water and carbon dioxide into sweet food for the plant.
Stores water and other vital liquids while giving the plant cell its rigid shape.
Provides a watery background where all the other cell parts float safely.
Acts as a flexible gatekeeper that lets helpful nutrients in while keeping harmful things out.

cellMembrane.description: A flexible outer barrier just inside the cell wall.
cellMembrane.function: Controls the movement of water, nutrients, and waste into and out of the cell.

cellWall.description: A tough, rigid outer layer made of cellulose that surrounds the cell membrane.
